top_cited_works.title: Label-Free Bond-Selective Imaging by Listening to Vibrationally Excited Molecules
top_cited_works.abstract: We report the realization of vibrational photoacoustic (VPA) microscopy using optical excitation of molecular overtone vibration and acoustic detection of the resultant pressure transients. Our approach eliminates the tissue scattering problem encountered in near-infrared spectroscopy and enables depth-resolved signal collection. The 2nd overtone of the CH bond stretch around 8300 cm(-1), where blood interference is minimal, is excited. We demonstrate 3D VPA imaging of lipid-rich atherosclerotic plaques by excitation from the artery lumen, and lipid storage in live Drosophila larvae, with millimeter scale penetration depth [corrected].

recent_works.title: Coherent Stokes Raman Scattering for Simultaneous Measurement of CO 2 and CH 4 Temperatures
recent_works.abstract: ABSTRACT Experimental measurements of fuel and flame temperatures in a methane/air co‐flow diffusion flame are performed using coherent Stokes Raman scattering. A three‐beam hybrid fs/ps configuration is employed such that the excitation bandwidth of the ultrafast pulses includes the rovibrational transitions in the Fermi‐dyad of CO and the mode of CH. Time‐domain spectroscopic models were developed and employed to simultaneously extract the CH and CO temperatures separately from the same CSRS spectra. Axial and radial temperature profiles of CH and CO in the diffusion flame are presented. Methane temperatures ranged from 300 to 900 K while CO temperatures ranged from 500 to 2500 K. At probe volume locations higher above the burner, the fuel and product temperatures were in strong agreement. Measurement locations near the methane injector revealed inhomogeneities between fuel and flame temperatures before significant mixing by diffusion. For the first time, a three‐beam ultrafast CSRS configuration is demonstrated to simultaneously measure differing CH and CO temperatures.

recent_works.title: One-dimensional time-resolved single-shot femtosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering thermometry in reacting thermal gradients
recent_works.abstract: Time-resolved thermometry is vital for quantitative characterization of reacting turbulent flows but remains largely limited to point measurements, making higher-dimensional approaches attractive for capturing spatiotemporal thermal gradients. In this work, a one-dimensional chirped-probe pulse coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) instrument has been developed for gas-phase thermometry. Calibration and characterization of the instrument are detailed, and its capability is demonstrated through measurements in a laboratory flame. The ro-vibrational transitions of N 2 are targeted in a uniform temperature flow field to calibrate the instrument and extract necessary laser parameters. The best-fit modeled laser parameters are examined in detail. Variations in laser parameters along the measurement line are captured and show dependence on non-uniform beam propagation and probe volume number density. After calibration, the instrument is successfully applied to a thermal gradient generated with a cooled-wall located perpendicular to the flow of the burner combustion products.

recent_works.title: Investigation of Flame Structure for Hydrogen Gas Turbine Combustion
recent_works.abstract: We have performed an investigation of flame structure and dynamics for gas turbine combustion with hydrogen (H2) and another hydrogen-based fuel, ammonia (NH3), and with mixtures of these fuels with natural gas. The objective of the research was to explore processes such as flame stabilization, ignition, and flashback, and to characterize combustion efficiency and pollutant emissions under combustion conditions characteristic of commercial aeroderivative and heavy-duty F- and H-class gas-turbine systems. Our research focused on a multi-stage, multi-tube micromixing (M3) injector with straight channels to carry the heated air and featuring staged transverse jet injection of fuels to vary the degree of premixing at the channel exit. The system was configured so that any of the three fuels, H2, NH3 or NG, or their blends, could be injected at any of the multiple injection locations. A test rig configured for combustion dynamics characterization with well-defined acoustic boundaries and high-frequency pressure instrumentation was used for the M3 injector experiments. recent_works.title: Methodology for Unsteady Exhaust Emissions Characterization in High-Pressure Hydrogen–Ammonia–Methane Flames
recent_works.abstract: A methodology for measuring and interpreting the influence of fuel composition on exhaust emissions in a high-pressure combustor operated with ammonia, methane and hydrogen fuels is investigated. A 19-element micro-mix multi-stage injector is used to introduce the fuel blend premixed with dry, heated air into an optically accessible combustor operating at 10 bar. In such systems, increasing ammonia concentration in the fuel blend can reduce combustion efficiency relative to equilibrium predictions, due to reduced kinetic rates and a corresponding decrease in Damköhler number when the ammonia fuel mole fraction exceeds 75\%. Accurate exhaust-gas composition is required to relate NO\textsubscript{x} formation to combustion efficiency and fuel-bound nitrogen pathways, making extractive gas measurements essential. In short-duration tests, chemical evolution in the sampling hardware, together with thermal and timing constraints on the sampling system, complicate the interpretation of measured exhaust composition as representative of combustor-exit conditions. recent_works.title: CUBRC 48” Tunnel Hypersonic Ground Testing of NOSpec
recent_works.abstract: Active control of hypersonic vehicles is a current area of research and development. Measurement of external flows around these vehicles can potentially be used as feedback for a control algorithm. To this end, a novel optical emission spectroscopy (OES) sensor called NOSpec was tested in the CUBRC LENS 48-inch reflected shock tunnel. NOSpec is a fiber coupled sensor utilizing a multi-anode photomultiplier tube array (MAPMT) as the detector to examine the external flow over a hypersonic vehicle. A blunt wedge with rounded corners and 10º half angle was used as the flight vehicle geometry for testing with a window placed on the blunt edge and a fiber collimator behind the window. These tests detected a noticeable change in NO signal from 0º angle of attack to 10º or 20º angle of attack while collecting information about the flow field. This work demonstrates the feasibility of the novel sensor architecture to non-intrusively detect changes in angle of attack, and it may be applied in the future for hypersonic vehicle active control.
